chunks.arabic_text: اَلْكَافِي: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى، عَنْ يُونُسَ، عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ، عَنِ الْحَارِثِ بْنِ الْمُغِيرَةِ النَّصْرِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ فِي قَوْلِ

translations.en: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira al-Nasri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the saying

chunks.arabic_text: اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: «إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى اللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ الْعُلَمَاءُ»

translations.en: Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Verily they truly fear Allah from among his slaves – the scholars”

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ: يَعْنِي بِالْعُلَمَاءِ مَنْ صَدَّقَ فِعْلُهُ قَوْلَهُ، وَمَنْ لَمْ يُصَدِّقْ فِعْلُهُ قَوْلَهُ فَلَيْسَ بِعَالِمٍ

translations.en: He said: He means by the scholars the one whose deeds conform with his words, as for the one whose deeds are contrary to his words then he is not a scholar.

en.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) explains the Quranic verse regarding who truly fears Allah. He defines true scholars not merely by their knowledge, but by the alignment of their actions with their words; those whose deeds contradict their words are not considered true scholars.
en.seo_question: What is the definition of a true scholar according to Imam al-Sadiq in this hadith?
